deviation_mechanism: The optimization routine displaced layer thicknesses from the stable 400.0 nm uniform baseline to a highly irregular distribution spanning 275.58 nm to 528.24 nm. In planar multilayer interferometry, optical performance depends on precise layer thicknesses to maintain constructive interference and impedance matching in the target band. Thicknesses exceeding 520 nm introduce excessive optical path difference, red/blue-shifting resonant peaks depending on layer index and leaking energy into adjacent bands, while compressions below 290 nm reduce layer optical density, breaking the intended phase progression. This combined phase accumulation error and spectral misalignment directly lowers the objective function value, explaining the observed ~0.049-point score degradation.
